Implemented and all hook checks pass.

**`gateway/gateway.go`** — `NewServer` builds a `ServeMux` over a defensive copy of the accounts (sorted by ID, plus an ID index) and returns a hardened `*http.Server`:

- `GET /healthz` → `ok`; `GET /accounts` → JSON array ordered by ID; `GET /accounts/{id}` → the object, 404 when unknown.
- `active` is accepted only as exactly `true` or `false` (one value); anything else — `1`, `TRUE`, empty, repeated — is a 400 whose body names the parameter. `strconv.ParseBool` would have let `1`/`t` through, so the comparison is literal.
- Every known path answers non-GET with 405 and an `Allow` header. `onlyGET` wraps the three handlers because a `GET` pattern in `ServeMux` otherwise serves `HEAD` with the GET handler's 200; everything else falls to the `/` catch-all 404.
- `encoding/json/v2` (Go 1.27 module) encodes a nil or fully filtered slice as `[]`, so both the empty and the no-match list stay arrays.
- Edge hardening, since the server faces the internet directly: `ReadHeaderTimeout` 5s, `ReadTimeout`/`WriteTimeout` 15s, `IdleTimeout` 30s, `MaxHeaderBytes` 64 KiB, `MaxHeaderValueCount` 64.

**`gateway/gateway_contract_test.go`** — one case per clause: routes and ordering, both `active` values and four rejected ones, unknown ID/path/subpath/trailing slash, `POST`/`HEAD`/`DELETE` on known paths, `POST` on an unknown path, plus the nil-accounts `[]` encoding, the caller-slice copy, and the timeout fields.

Notes on the decisions the documentation forced:
- A `GET` pattern answers `HEAD` with 200 by default; the contract makes every non-GET method a 405, so a `HEAD` pattern is registered beside each `GET` route. Non-GET, non-HEAD methods get the mux's own 405. Unknown paths stay 404 for every method, since no catch-all is registered.
- `active` accepts only `true`/`false`, not `strconv.ParseBool`'s `t`/`1`/`TRUE`; `?active=` (present but empty) is also a 400 naming the parameter.
- The accounts slice is snapshotted and sorted into a new slice, so the caller's slice is never reordered; `encoding/json/v2` encodes the empty result as `[]`, not `null`.
